event_confirmation: Company press release of 2026-10-07 (GlobeNewswire, carried by QuiverQuant and EarningsWhispers): Q3 2026 results released after the close of business on 2026-10-21, call 2026-10-22 10:00 EDT. Event date and amc session both settled by the company itself; the sweep had NOT confirmed them. One aggregator (Unusual Whales) shows 2026-10-28, which the company release contradicts. https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Eagle+Bancorp+Announces+Third+Quarter+2026+Earnings+Conference+Call
conviction_note: Balanced evidence. On one side are a known $5.3m Maryland tax benefit and management's H2 provision relief, which together make a GAAP headline beat of the $0.34-0.35 consensus likely, plus a 14.6% CET1 at 0.76x TBV with no buyback and a 10%-of-shares short. On the other side are Q2 30-89 day past dues that went from $18.0m to $44.1m, a FY NIM guide of 2.6-2.7% that needs an H2 step-up from 2.52%, and a new CEO's first full quarter. p_up is 52 on abs_move 7, so the scaled number is +0.28. The findings sum to -0.10. The gap is sign noise around zero, not a disagreement.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.34 (Benzinga https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/EGBN/earnings-forecasts) and $0.35 (EarningsWhispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/EGBN). Two sources agree within a cent. Revenue consensus is dispersed ($65.8m to $77.0m across sources), so it is not a usable bar. Unresolved: whether the $0.35 includes the $5.3m (~$0.17/share) discrete tax benefit flagged in the Q2 10-Q. The findings that depend on that point are capped small. No company EPS guide. The company guides FY2026 NIM 2.6-2.7%, noninterest expense -7% to -11% and noninterest income +15% to +25% (https://reportify.cn/news/1277825936850685952).
positioning_check: Short interest 3,147,985 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 10.33% of shares outstanding (30.48m), days to cover 8.13. Up from 2,682,284 (8.80%) at 2026-07-31, so shorts built through Q3 into the print (Equibles from FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/egbn/shortinterest). The baseline has no usable option chain: unusable_chain, ATM spread 194% of mid, no skew, open interest 169. The market has made no directional statement. Spot $28.55 is 2% below the 52-week high and 80.7% above the low, up 4.0% over 5 days and 1.75% over 20 days. Moderately crowded short into a name at its highs: negatives shrunk for squeeze risk.

findings.finding: The Q2 2026 10-Q subsequent-events note says Eagle settled its Maryland corporate income tax refund claims for 2019-2020 on 2026-07-21 and expects a discrete tax benefit of about $5.3m in Q3 2026. That is about $0.17/share on 30.48m shares, or roughly half of the $0.34-0.35 EPS consensus. It is a below-the-line one-off with no path to guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior tax one-off on this name in the baseline. On Q2 (2026-07-22) a GAAP EPS miss ($0.23 vs $0.34-0.355) driven by provisions brought +2.45% close to close. Holders looked through below-the-line items in the headline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed, so careful analysts know it. Aggregator consensus may or may not include it: the two sources at $0.34/$0.35 give no adjusted/GAAP split. If it were fully in the bar, consensus would imply a Q3 provision near the Q2 level of $21.4m, which contradicts guidance (see the provision finding). If it is outside the bar, GAAP EPS prints a mechanical ~$0.17 beat. Either way it is a one-off and sized small.
findings.independence: Panabee's Q2 10-Q digest repeats the $5.3m benefit (https://www.panabee.com/news/eagle-earnings-q2-2026-report, 2026-08-06), but it rests on the same 10-Q, so this is one document. Quartr's call summary also cites it (https://quartr.com/events/eagle-bancorp-inc-egbn-q2-2026_ozUdE1aA).

findings.finding: Management expects lower provisions in H2 2026 than Q2's $21.4m, and Q2 PPNR was $29.1m (rising from $27.7m). With PPNR flat and the provision in the low teens, core EPS ex-tax lands near $0.40-0.45. That compares with a $0.34-0.35 consensus which, if it carries the tax benefit, implies a provision near $22m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Provision drove the Q2 miss and the stock still rose +2.45%. Q4 2025 (2026-01-21) brought +16.0% and Q1 2026 brought -2.72%. During the 2025 credit cycle provision-driven prints moved -11% to -21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is near its 52-week high, so the market believes credit is stabilizing. The arithmetic gap between the guide and the consensus is not visible in any preview I found. The bar's construction (GAAP including or excluding tax) is unresolved, so the finding is capped small.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K PPNR $29.1m and provision $21.4m: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050441/000105044126000088/final-erq2x2026xearnings.htm. The 'lower H2 provision' claim comes from a search summary of EarningsWhispers/Webull (snippet_only), not the transcript. Reportify's call summary says no explicit provision forecast was given (https://reportify.cn/news/1277825936850685952). That conflict is part of why this is small.

findings.finding: Leading credit indicators deteriorated in Q2 even as NPLs fell. Loans 30-89 days past due rose to $44.1m from $18.0m, NPL inflows were $36.0m and substandard loans rose to $459.8m from $447.6m. NPLs fell only because $47.9m of NCOs (2.78% annualized) came from dispositions. That points to new migration into NPL and NCO in Q3, against a 7.22% performing-office reserve and an ACL down to 1.83% of loans.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline in July was NPLs down $17.7m and criticized loans down $34.5m, and the stock is now 2% off its 52-week high, so the market reads credit as healing. If the past-due jump were priced, the stock would not sit at its highs with an 80% rally off the low. The crowded short (10% of shares) is the one place this view is expressed, and that is why the size is shrunk.
findings.independence: Peer read: Atlantic Union (DC/MD/VA footprint) Q3 release on 2026-10-20 shows accruing past dues up to 0.34% from 0.28%, led by CRE non-owner-occupied (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000883948/000088394826000077/aub-ex99d1.htm). Its NCOs stayed 0.03%. Proxy only.

findings.finding: FY2026 NIM guide is 2.60-2.70%, but Q1 was 2.47% and Q2 2.52%, so H2 must average about 2.70% (low end) to 2.90% (high end). Q3 NIM therefore needs a step-up of about 15-20bp. DC-area peer Atlantic Union's cost of funds rose 7bp in Q3, and the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. A Q3 NIM near 2.55% would likely force a cut to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM guide narrowed (not cut) in Q2 and the stock rose +2.45%. No NIM-guide cut in the baseline window to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: Management attributed the shortfall in Q2's 2.52% to a one-time loan-sale effect and kept the range, so consensus is likely modelling the step-up. The Fed hike and peer deposit-cost creep came after Eagle last spoke. If the market doubted the guide, consensus revenue would not run as high as $72-77m.
findings.independence: Fed hike: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm. AUB cost of funds +7bp to 2.01%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000883948/000088394826000077/aub-ex99d1.htm. Eagle's own rate sensitivity was not sourced, so the transmission is a proxy. Quartr says Q2 NIM was depressed by a one-time loan-sale effect (https://quartr.com/events/eagle-bancorp-inc-egbn-q2-2026_ozUdE1aA), which argues the step-up is partly mechanical.

findings.finding: Capital is idle and the stock is cheap against it. CET1 is 14.58% (up from 13.80%) and TCE 11.91%. TBV is $37.73/share against a $28.55 spot, or 0.76x. The dividend is $0.01, and no repurchase appears in the 10-Q equity statements. Management said on the Q2 call it is 'evaluating capital levels, flexibility, and ways to create long-term shareholder value', and Q3 is new CEO Curley's first full quarter. A buyback authorization or dividend increase is a live possibility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return announcement in the baseline window. The last authorization was December 2022 (1.6m shares).
findings.why_not_priced: No authorization exists and no preview I found expects one. At 0.76x TBV, a priced buyback would show as a narrower TBV discount. The stock's rally may partly anticipate it, so the size is kept modest.
findings.independence: Capital-evaluation quote from the call summary: https://reportify.cn/news/1277825936850685952. 10-Q equity statement shows no repurchases: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050441/000105044126000096/egbn-20260630.htm.

findings.finding: Stephen Curley became CEO effective 2026-07-06 and joined the Risk Committee on 2026-09-14. Q3 is his first full quarter, the classic window for a reserve build or bulk disposition of office/classified loans. Q2 NCOs ($47.9m) already came mainly from dispositions, so a cleanup has started.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Disposition-driven Q2 NCOs coincided with a +2.45% reaction: holders rewarded cleanup.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from timing, not a document. Q2 already carried the new CEO's influence, and the market rewarded it, so a further sink may be read as positive. Sized small, with a wide downside tail.
findings.independence: None independent. It shares the Q2 8-K with the past-due finding, and its sign is offset by the Q2 reaction.

findings.finding: DC office market improved in Q3 2026. CBRE reports 360,154 sq ft of positive absorption and a 40bp drop in overall vacancy (Q2 overall vacancy ~22.2%). Eagle has about $533m of office exposure, of which about $77m is criticized or classified per a Q2 10-Q digest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The office-credit line drove the 2025 double-digit drops. Improvement prints since (+16.0%, +2.45%) rose.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public market series and likely part of why the stock is at its highs. It is a proxy for collateral values, not Eagle's own book, so it is sized small. Cushman & Wakefield reports year-to-date leasing down 9% (https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/insights/us-marketbeats/washington-dc-marketbeats/office), which tempers it.
findings.independence: Office exposure figures: https://www.panabee.com/news/eagle-earnings-q2-2026-report (AI-generated digest; not checked against the 10-Q body).

findings.finding: Short interest built through Q3, from 2.68m shares (8.80%) at 2026-07-31 to 3.15m (10.33% of shares outstanding) at 2026-09-30, with days to cover at 8.1-14.4 over the period. A credit-clean print or a capital-return announcement meets a positioned short that needs about 8 days of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +16.0% on 2026-01-21 came into a similarly shorted name. Q2's +2.45% came on an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is a position, not a forecast. It amplifies whichever way the credit lines land, and it skews the reaction to a good print up. If it had already been covered, the September settlements would show declines, not increases.
findings.independence: CurvedTrading (FINRA-sourced) shows 2.8m short and DTC 12.1 at 2026-08-14, consistent with this (snippet_only, page 403).

findings.finding: EagleBank signed a one-year non-prosecution agreement with DOJ / USAO Middle District of Pennsylvania (dated 2026-06-30). The ~$9.8m BSA penalty was fully accrued in 2025, but compliance obligations may keep noninterest expense elevated for about 12 months. That pressures the -7% to -11% FY expense guide at the margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolable. The settlement was announced 2026-07-01, before the Q2 print, which then rose +2.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: The penalty is priced and accrued. Only the ongoing compliance-cost tail is possibly underappreciated, and the expense guide was reaffirmed after the settlement, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Expense-elevation note: https://www.panabee.com/news/eagle-earnings-q2-2026-report (AI digest). Company 8-K language 'fully accrued in 2025': https://www.sahmcapital.com/news/content/eagle-bancorp-says-its-subsidiary-eaglebank-reaches-settlement-with-us-attorneys-office-for-middle-district-of-pennsylvania-co-to-pay-about-98m-under-settlement-fully-accrued-in-2025-2026-07-01

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The stock is at its 52-week high after an 80% rally, which prices credit stabilization: the past-due and NIM negatives cut against the run-up, while the capital and short-squeeze positives run with it. Net is close to balanced.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): Maryland tax benefit cut from +0.5 to +0.3. It is below the line with no path to guidance.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced from two agreeing estimates, but whether it includes the tax benefit is unresolved. The provision-vs-consensus finding that depends on it is capped from +1.0 to +0.6.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): with 10.3% of shares short and DTC 8.1, the past-due negative goes from -1.5 to -1.2 and the CEO kitchen-sink negative from -0.5 to -0.4.

Rules 1, 5 and 4 left standing: NIM guide (-1.0, company guide arithmetic plus proxies), capital (+1.0), DC office proxy (+0.3, already small), short positioning (+0.5) and BSA expense tail (-0.2) unchanged. abs_move and p_up unchanged.
